items.title: The Stock Market Is Finally Rising Again—and It’s Getting Cheaper, Too
items.summary: In a “shrinkflation” world, investors might want to stop and appreciate the stock market, which is giving them more for less.  While the  is up 22% in the past year, valuations have actually come down, with the forward price/earnings ratio falling from 22.1 times forward earnings to 20 times, per Bloomberg data.  Simply put, the “E” is rising faster than the “P.” Second-quarter earnings season has been one for the ages, with 86% of companies beating earnings estimates, above the average of 78%, and S&P 500 companies growing earnings by a startling 50.4% from one year ago, per FactSet.

items.title: Alphabet (GOOGL) Lines Up $25 Billion Bond Offering For AI Expansion
items.summary: Alphabet (NasdaqGS: GOOGL) announces a US$25b bond offering to fund AI expansion following its first recorded period of negative free cash flow. The debt deal marks a shift in Alphabet's capital structure as it leans on bond markets to support large scale AI infrastructure investment. The move comes while Google DeepMind faces executive turnover, leadership reshuffles and delays in certain AI model releases.
